preamble: Debuccalization of [g] to the glottal fricative [h] is a common form of lenition, notably found in Galician (Gheada) and Southern Dutch dialects, and in Czech, Slovak, Ukrainian and Belarusian, where Proto-Slavic *g became [ɦ].

examples.note: Proto-Slavic *g became the glottal fricative [ɦ] (written h) in Czech, Slovak, Upper Sorbian, Ukrainian and Belarusian.
Gheada debuccalizes /ɡ/ to a voiceless back fricative, often [ħ] or [h].

sources: Sussex, R., & Cubberley, P. (2006). The Slavic Languages. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511486807
